Operator: Good day, and welcome to the Apex Asset Management Q2 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. As a reminder, during the Q&A session, please press star one if you would like to register for a question. Please be advised that today's conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera: Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss Apex Asset Management's Q2 2024 results. Joining me on today's call are Mark Thompson, Chief Executive Officer; Lisa Chen, Chief Financial Officer; David Patel, Chief Investment Officer; Sarah Jenkins, Head of Distribution; Mike Lopez, Head of Operations; and Elena Vasquez, Head of Risk Management.

Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that some of the statements made today may be forward-looking. Please refer to our SEC filings for a discussion of the risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially.

With that, I'll turn the call over to Mark Thompson.

Mark Thompson: Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us. I'm pleased to report on our performance for Q2 2024. We achieved solid results this quarter, driven by robust market appreciation and record net inflows. Our AUM grew to $1.2 trillion.

Lisa Chen: Thank you, Mark. From a financial perspective, Apex Asset Management delivered strong results in Q2 2024. Our revenue was $4.8 billion, representing a 12% increase quarter-over-quarter and 22% year-over-year. This growth was primarily driven by the critical linkage between our assets under management and top-line revenue performance. As you know, in our industry, revenue is predominantly fee-driven, with roughly 85% of our topline coming from management fees calculated on average daily AUM at our blended fee rate of 42 basis points, down just 1 basis point from last quarter due to ongoing fee compression in our beta equity strategies, supplemented by performance fees from our alternatives book and ancillary revenues from distribution and advisory services. Changes in AUM—whether from market movements, net client flows, or strategic product shifts—have a direct, leveraged impact on our earnings power.

Ending AUM reached $1.2 trillion as of June 30th, up 8% quarter-over-quarter and 15% year-over-year. This was driven by a 4% market appreciation tailwind, primarily from the S&P 500's 5.2% gain and the MSCI EAFE's 3.8% rally amid cooling inflation data and expectations of a Fed pivot. Overlaying that, we posted record net inflows of $25 billion—our strongest quarter since Q4 2021—translating to 2.1% organic growth on beginning AUM. This outpaced peers like T. Rowe Price, who reported flat flows, and even BlackRock's ETF juggernaut, which saw $18 billion in ETF inflows but modest mutual fund outflows.

Total fee-related revenue hit $4.8 billion, reflecting average AUM for the quarter at $1.15 trillion—up 7% quarter-over-quarter—multiplied by our blended management fee rate. That's a straightforward revenue formula: Revenue ≈ Average AUM × Blended Fee Rate × (Days in Period / 365). The 7% AUM lift alone contributed about $320 million in incremental fees, or about 65% of our quarter-over-quarter revenue growth. Performance fees added another $150 million, up 40% quarter-over-quarter, fueled by 12% realized gains in our $180 billion private markets platform, where carried interest from exits in tech and infrastructure deals—like our co-investment in a renewable energy fund alongside KKR—kicked in.

To quantify sensitivity: Our revenue is highly elastic to AUM. A 1% change in average AUM typically drives $45-50 million in annual fee revenue at current rates. We've stress-tested this: In a +10% equity market scenario with the S&P to 6,000, we'd see about $80 billion in AUM uplift and $400 million in added FY24 revenue. Conversely, a 10% drawdown—like the 2022 bear market—shaved $90 billion off our AUM and compressed revenues by 15%. This quarter's market beta was positive, but we mitigated volatility through our 60/40 active-passive mix.

Regionally, North America, our largest franchise at 55% of AUM or $660 billion, grew 10% quarter-over-quarter on $15 billion in inflows, led by SMAs and 401(k) wrap programs. Clients rotated into our low-cost active ETFs, like the Apex Core Equity ETF (APEXQ), which gathered $8 billion amid Vanguard-style passive momentum but with our alpha overlay. Europe, at 25% of AUM or $300 billion, saw 5% growth but softer 1.5% organic flows due to MiFID II redemption pressures and outflows from high-fee UCITS funds—$3 billion net redemptions. We countered with fee rebates and our new sustainable ESG suite, capturing €5 billion in AUM from continental platforms. APAC was the star, up 12% to $180 billion or 15% of total, driven by 3% organic growth from HNW wealth platforms in Hong Kong and Singapore. Inflows totaled $7 billion, including RMB-denominated products hedging CNY depreciation. This reflects broader trends: Asia's $20 trillion wealth transfer by 2030, per UBS estimates, favoring alternatives like our long-short hedge fund feeder, up 20% AUM on 15% NAV performance.

Longer-term, AUM growth has compounded at 9% CAGR since 2019, outpacing the industry's 7% per PwC Global AUM Report. But fee compression persists: Our equity fees fell to 35 basis points from 38 basis points year-over-year, mirroring BlackRock's iShares trajectory, as ETFs now represent 40% of our book, up from 30%. Fixed income fees held at 22 basis points, resilient amid inverted curves, while alts averaged 95 basis points—our margin engine.

We're not passive observers. To drive durable AUM growth and defend fees: We've rolled out Apex FlowOne, our Aladdin-inspired tech stack with API integrations for $10 billion quarterly inflows via embedded finance partnerships like with Wealthfront and Schwab, boosting organic growth by 50 basis points. We've launched 15 new outsourced CIO mandates, aggregating $20 billion in institutional AUM from pensions, with AI-driven personalization reducing churn by 20%. We're targeting 25% of AUM in alternatives by 2026 from 15%, with evergreen PE funds and credit opportunities funds drawing $5 billion quarter-over-quarter. Performance fees here could double as dry powder deploys amid normalizing rates. We've hedged 20% of equity AUM with overlays, limiting drawdown impact to 60% of market beta.

Looking forward, we guide to $10-12 billion in long-term net flows for FY24, assuming MSCI World +5-7%. Risks include prolonged high rates pressuring fixed income AUM, 25% of book, and geopolitical flows from EM. But with our diversified franchise—active equities 35%, passives 40%, FI 20%, alts 15%—we're positioned for mid-teens revenue growth.

Our expenses were $1.45 billion for the first half of 2024, up 7.2% year-over-year from $1.35 billion in H1 2023. This increase reflects cost discipline amid robust AUM growth—our assets under management reached $1.2 trillion as of June 30th, up 15% year-over-year—while investing in high-ROI areas like digital transformation and talent to support long-term fee compression pressures in our ETF and index strategies. On a GAAP basis, our expense ratio—operating expenses as a percentage of average AUM—improved to 28 basis points from 30 basis points in H1 2023, demonstrating leverage from scale advantages, particularly in low-cost passive products like our Apex Core S&P 500 ETF, which now holds over $150 billion in AUM and mirrors efficiency at peers like Vanguard and BlackRock's iShares suite. Excluding non-recurring items such as a $25 million one-time restructuring charge related to our EMEA footprint optimization, core operating expenses rose a more modest 5.8% year-over-year.

Breaking this down by key categories: Compensation and benefits totaled $785 million, 54% of total OpEx, up 9.1% year-over-year. This remains our largest line item in a talent-intensive industry where human capital drives alpha in active equity and alternatives strategies. The increase was driven by a 6% rise in headcount to 4,200 full-time equivalents, focused on bolstering quant and data science teams amid the AI boom—enhancements to our proprietary Apex Alpha platform, akin to BlackRock's Aladdin but tailored for multi-asset class risk modeling. Base salaries grew 4.2% on average, but variable comp, tied to 12% revenue growth and strong performance in our private markets group, up 18% year-over-year AUM to $180 billion, pushed deferred incentives higher. Wage inflation moderated to 3-4% in the US, but APAC talent markets remain competitive, with costs up 12% in Singapore and Tokyo hubs due to demand for ESG integration specialists. US compensation accounted for 62% of this bucket, EMEA rose 15% due to MiFID II-compliant remuneration disclosures. We're ahead on retention with a new long-term incentive plan emphasizing clawbacks and ESG-linked metrics, targeting turnover below 8% versus industry average of 12%.

Technology and data services: $220 million, 15% of total, up 15% year-over-year. This underscores commitment to operational resilience and innovation, including $85 million in cloud migration to AWS and Snowflake for scalable data lakes supporting our robo-advisor platform, Apex Direct, serving 2.5 million retail clients with $45 billion AUM—growth fueled by zero-commission trading post-GameStop volatility. $40 million invested in gen-AI pilots for portfolio optimization, reducing model recalibration time by 40% in fixed income strategies amid the Fed's rate-cutting cycle; enhanced cybersecurity following SEC Reg S-P updates. Breakdown: Software licenses and data feeds like Bloomberg and Refinitiv at 45%, personnel 30%, capex amortization 25%. APAC saw 22% growth due to localization for China's QDII quotas. As a percentage of revenue, this ticked up to 8 basis points of AUM from 7 basis points, but we expect stabilization at 9 basis points by FYE as AI efficiencies compound, similar to State Street's trajectory.

General and administrative: $195 million, 13% of total, flat year-over-year. Held steady through vendor consolidation and remote-hybrid work models at 65% of workforce. Office rationalization saved $15 million, including subleasing legacy Chicago space. Travel and facilities dipped 8% post-pandemic, offset by 5% uptick in professional fees for audit and tax amid global minimum tax reforms like Pillar Two. Regulatory compliance rose modestly to $45 million, covering FINRA exams and EU SFDR reporting—critical as 25% of our $180 billion sustainable strategies face enhanced disclosures.

Distribution, marketing, and servicing: $170 million, 12% of total, up 4% year-over-year. Reflects targeted spend to capture market share in high-growth channels. Sub-advisory fees to platforms like Schwab and Fidelity grew with ETF lineup, now 40% of AUM. Marketing ramped 7% for digital campaigns promoting our Apex Alternatives Fund targeting millennial HNWIs via LinkedIn and podcast sponsorships, servicing costs for 401(k) wrap programs ticked up with participant growth. EMEA distribution rose 10% on post-Brexit integrations, US wholesaling efficiency improved via CRM automation, keeping cost-to-sales at 15%.

Amortization, depreciation, and other: $80 million, 6% of total, down 2% year-over-year. Primarily amortization of intangibles from our 2022 acquisition of a private equity firm, $30 million run-rate, depreciation steady on data center upgrades. Other includes $10 million in bad debt provisions tied to credit hedge fund exposures during regional bank mini-crisis.

Looking ahead, we guide full-year OpEx to $2.95-3.05 billion, implying 6-8% growth, with expense ratio at 27-29 basis points of AUM assuming year-end growth. Tailwinds: AI-driven automation targeting 5-7% productivity gains in PM and ops; scale from ETF inflows amid VIX averaging 18 in Q2; disciplined hiring with 1:15 portfolio manager-to-AUM ratio. Headwinds include inflation in comp at 4.5% and regulatory tailwinds like SEC T+1. Regionally, optimizing EMEA 18% of OpEx via shared services in Dublin, leaning into APAC 20% AUM CAGR. Compared to peers—BlackRock at 25 basis points, T. Rowe at 32 basis points—our efficiency enables reinvestment into differentiated products like tokenised real assets on blockchain.

This resulted in net income of $2.5 billion. Our expense ratio improved due to scale leverage and cost discipline. Management fees for the quarter came in at $452 million, up 9% year-over-year and 3% quarter-over-quarter, marking our 11th consecutive quarter of growth, driven by 12% increase in average AUM to $758 billion within our total, partially offset by modest fee compression. For full year, tracking towards $1.8 billion, 10% increase from 2023.

Net inflows totaled $18 billion for the quarter within the broader $25 billion, with $12 billion in long-term skewed to higher-margin alternatives and multi-asset. Equities $8 billion fueled by active large-cap growth outperforming S&P 500 by 250 basis points net. Fixed income $5 billion from reallocations amid Fed pause. $2 billion outflows from low-margin legacy index as rotation to active SMAs.

North America 62% of AUM at $470 billion, fees up 11% on institutional DC plans and wirehouses. EMEA 7% fee growth to $152 million on €15 billion UCITS ESG inflows capturing from Amundi, DWS amid SFDR. APAC standout 18% to $68 million on A$20 billion sovereign allocations to private credit. EM 8% of AUM fees up 14% on commodity EM equity.

Average fee rates ticked down 2 basis points quarter-over-quarter to 45.2 basis points, 1 basis point YoY to 47 basis points TTM. Reflects compression in beta equity/core FI where Vanguard/BlackRock ETFs push below 10 basis points. Institutional 3 basis points pressure from RFPs, tiered to 35-40 basis points on large mandates. Retail wrapped steady at 62 basis points.

Proactively managing via mix shift: Alternatives 22% AUM up from 18%, 85 basis points average including 1.2% on direct lending PE closing $4.5 billion at blended 1.45% plus 15 basis points committed. $25 million performance fees from hedge composites at 12% net.

Fee Optimization Initiative with Aladdin-like analytics, AI client segmentation stabilizes renewals at 92%, dynamic pricing bundling overlays preserving 5-10 basis points. Scaling ETF wrappers around active; Apex Active Equity ETF $3 billion at 28 basis points attracted $1.2 billion YTD. $1.2 billion acquisition of alternatives brings $45 billion niche real assets at 70 basis points, accretive 300 basis points blended. ESG/thematic 15% AUM at 55 basis points premium. Expect 46-47 basis points through 2025 with 8-10% AUM growth from $25-30 billion inflows, $150 billion pipeline.

For performance fees realized, we recognized $285 million in the quarter, up 42% quarter-over-quarter and 68% year-over-year, trailing 12-month $1.12 billion or 12% of total fee revenue above 9% long-term average. Surge from equity long/short and private credit hitting high-water marks/hurdles. Structured 20% carry above 6% preferred/benchmark, annual crystallization mostly, quarterly hedge composites.

Equity long/short $142 million from Apex Alpha Equity Fund outperforming S&P 500 by 1,200 basis points net YTD. Alternatives $78 million from private markets, Direct Lending V realizations exceeding 8% LIBOR-plus. Fixed income $45 million from CLO equity amid wider spreads. Offsets management fee pressure from ETF outflows, revenue mix 55% base/45% performance superior to T. Rowe/Franklin at 30-35%.

78% of AUM beat benchmarks 3-year annualized net. Equities $220 billion composite 18.2% YTD vs S&P 500 15.4% by 280 basis points. Large-cap growth 22.1% vs Russell 1000 Growth 19.8% on NVIDIA/ASML. Value 12.5% vs 10.2%. US Sharpe 1.45, Europe 11.8% beat MSCI Europe 150 basis points, EM 14.2% vs 9.7%. Fixed income $120 billion 4.8% vs BB Agg 1.2% by 360 basis points, duration shortened to 4.2 years. HY 9.1% vs 7.6%, muni 5.2% vs 2.1%. Alts PE 12.5% IRR vs median 10.2%, multi-asset 11.3% vs 9.8%.

Quant Alpha Engine 2.0 covers 85% equity enhancing factors; ESG 65% AUM +50 basis points green premia; risk parity reduced drawdowns 15%. Launching UCITS long/short, interval private credit for $10 billion inflows. Opportunities in quality cyclicals, duration extension.

Compensation ratio at 47.2% quarter, 210 basis points improvement YoY from 49.3%, sequential from 48.5% Q1, H1 47.8% pacing mid-47% full-year ahead of 48-50% guide. Cornerstone of operating leverage where talent drives alpha vs revenue from AUM/fee dynamics. Comp expense $1.42 billion Q2 up 8% YoY but revenue +22% to $3.01 billion on $18 billion inflows, S&P +15% YTD, AUM $1.2 trillion +12% YoY, ETF fee revenue $2.1 billion +25%.

Fixed comp 28% total or 13.2% revenue, headcount flat 4,200 post-2023 restructuring consolidating research -15% layers. Variable 72% up 12% to $1.02 billion on Pinnacle Global Alpha 18% net vs MSCI World +650 basis points triggering incentives.

Americas 62% revenue ratio 46.1% scale $850 billion US wealth $12 billion 401(k) rollovers ETF 18 basis points. Europe 22% revenue 50.4% higher alts private credit 12% IRR offset MiFID research unbundling. APAC 16% 48.7% investments HK/Singapore chase $5 trillion RMB, Japan equity compresses 300 basis points YoY.

AI Pinnacle Insights automates 40% quant tasks reallocating 150 analysts, 5% efficiency +200 basis points target year-end. Blockchain attribution for $200 billion SMA precise deferrals LTIP 60% stock clawbacks. Variable moderates if perf fees soften, competitive vs Citadel >55%, BlackRock sub-45%, 25%+ EPS growth 2024.

David Patel: Thank you, Lisa. On the investment front, we continue to focus on delivering strong risk-adjusted returns for our clients. Our key strategies performed well, particularly in equities and alternatives. We are navigating the current market environment by tactically overweighting U.S. large-cap tech and European defensives, leveraging our Quant Alpha Engine and ESG integration. We launched several new products this quarter, including the Apex Sustainable Global Equity ETF (ESGE), Apex Active Duration Fixed Income Fund (ADFI), and Apex Private Credit Opportunities Fund (PCOF), and the early reception has been positive, with $2.8 billion in initial AUM and $1.2 billion net inflows representing 15% of quarterly organic growth.

Fiscal Q3—aligned to our cycle—marked our most active for launches in two years, five new vehicles. ESGE on NYSE Arca, top-decile MSCI ESG seeking 200-300 basis points alpha over MSCI World SRI at 0.28% ER below BlackRock's, $1.1 billion AUM $850 million wirehouses, +12.4% YTD +320 basis points benchmark. ADFI UCITS intermediate corporates/EM debt YTM 5.8% duration 4.2 years post BB Global Agg +2.1%, $750 million including €400 million EU pensions Solvency II. PCOF semi-liquid interval 9-11% IRR mid-market tech/healthcare, $450 million tapping $1.7 trillion dry powder per Preqin, $300 million RIAs BBB spreads 125 basis points. Asia ex-Japan Small Cap $250 million, Target 2050 ETF $250 million quant factors.

Underpinned by Apex AI Optimizer integrating alt data satellite/NLP, -40% model drift Sharpe 1.2-1.5. APAC 45% inflows $1.25 billion MAS incentives China reopening, EMEA 30% UCITS, Americas RIA great wealth transfer $84 trillion Cerulli.

150+ funds 78% AUM top-quartile Lipper 3/5-year, 62 funds 4/5-star Morningstar $145 billion 55% FUM ahead industry 48%, vs T. Rowe 58% Fidelity 52%. Large Cap Growth +18.7% vs Russell +15.2% +350 bps 5/5 stars 1st Lipper; EM Equity +11.5% vs MSCI +8.9% +260 bps 4/5 2nd; Core Bond +4.2% vs Agg +2.8% +140 bps 5/4 1st; Global Real Assets +9.8% vs S&P +7.1% +270 bps 5/5 1st. Equities avg +210 bps, FI +110, alts +450 IRR. Sharpe 1.1 vs 0.9 cat, drawdown -8.2% Aug. Japan underperformer stemmed outflows 2% AUM.

Positioned mid-teens AUM growth FY24 $300 billion target from $265 billion base, smart beta hybrids defend 28% active. Retention 96%, DC +22% YoY. Q4 Crypto-Linked Balanced ETF, AI Infrastructure UCITS Nvidia/ECB. Partnerships Schwab/Fidelity.

Sarah Jenkins: Thank you, David. From a distribution perspective, we saw strong inflows into our ETF and alternatives funds. Our efforts to expand our reach in APAC and EMEA are paying off, as evidenced by robust organic growth from HNW platforms, sovereign allocations, and UCITS launches capturing share amid regulatory tailwinds.

Mike Lopez: Thank you, Sarah. Operationally, we've made significant progress in improving our technology infrastructure, including cloud migrations, gen-AI pilots, and cybersecurity enhancements. This has resulted in increased efficiency and reduced operational risk. We are also focused on vendor consolidation, office rationalization, and shared services to sustain expense leverage.

Elena Vasquez: Thank you, Mike. From a risk management perspective, we continue to maintain a robust framework to identify, assess, and mitigate risks across the organization. We have enhanced our monitoring of market volatility and geopolitical exposures and are taking steps to address potential vulnerabilities. This includes volatility targeting, hedging overlays on 20% equity AUM, and high-water mark protections in performance vehicles.

Mark Thompson: In summary, we are confident in our ability to continue delivering value to our shareholders. We are focused on executing our strategic priorities and capitalizing on the opportunities ahead. This includes guiding to mid-teens organic growth in FY24 accelerating to 15-18% FY25 assuming normalized markets, Fed 75-100 basis points cuts, to $1.5 trillion FY24-end $1.8 trillion mid-FY26. Organic $110-130 billion net new money FY24 building $95 billion FY23, ETFs 28% AUM $18 billion quarterly flows HDIV +120 bps YTD, retail/RIA +25% QoQ Horizon Alpha AI tax-alpha 97% retention. Institutional $40-50 billion pensions alts, Private Credit V $12 billion oversubscribed 40% 12-15% IRR Blackstone/Ares tailwinds. Market 8-10% MSCI World 7-9% active alpha 150-200 bps.

Inorganic $200-300 million bolt-ons like $15 billion European quant tuck-in enhancing direct indexing 42 bps fee. North America 62% 10-12% HNW/family offices; Europe 22% 18-20% UCITS ETF €4 billion EuroStoxx Climate; APAC 12% 25%+ CAGR DBS JV Sharia sukuk China A-shares EM double India/LatAm IMF reforms. Fee compression passive 25 bps offset active/alts 55 bps +2% YoY privates pricing.

Tech blockchain NAV predictive flows Q1'25 -15% ops sub-1% TER; ESG 35% flows Sustainable Income $20 billion 18 months PIMCO green; distribution model Envestnet/Orion robo 500k retail. Risks equity derating P/E 21x inflation 5% beta; geopolitics EM. Diversified 45% eq 30% FI 20% alts 5% cash dry powder 8%. Bridge: $1.2T +$120B NNM 9% mkt/FX $20B inorganic $1.52T FY24; FY25 +2% NNM/100bps eq, margins +50bps to 38% alts.

Operator: Thank you. We will now begin the question and answer session. Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs.

John Smith: Good morning. Can you provide more details on management fee trends and fee rate pressures?

Mark Thompson: Thanks John. As Lisa detailed, we're navigating compression proactively with mix shift to alts at 85 bps and ESG premiums, holding blended 46-47 bps through 2025 on strong pipeline.

John Smith: Thank you. And a follow-up on your AUM growth outlook specifics?

Lisa Chen: Happy to. Mid-teens organic FY24 $110-130B NNM, sensitivities +2% per 100bps equity upside, margins expand on alts weighting.

Operator: Our next question comes from Emily Davis with Morningstar.

Emily Davis: Good morning. Could you elaborate on the performance of the Apex Alpha Equity Fund?

David Patel: Absolutely Emily. Our equity long/short like AAEF generated $142 million perf fees outperforming S&P by 1,200 bps net YTD, part of 78% AUM top-quartile, Sharpe 1.45 US, broad alpha from quant/ESG/risk parity.

Emily Davis: And how is the new product Apex Sustainable Global Equity ETF performing relative to expectations?

Sarah Jenkins: Exceeding, Emily. ESGE $1.1B AUM +12.4% YTD +320 bps MSCI SRI, $850M wirehouses, leading our thematic expansion tapping millennial wealth transfer and MAS/SFDR tailwinds.

Operator: Our next question comes from Robert Lee with JPMorgan.

Robert Lee: Can you provide more color on the operational efficiencies you've gained?

Mike Lopez: Sure Robert. AI pilots cut recalibration 40%, cloud/data lakes scale robo to 2.5M clients, vendor/office savings $15M, targeting 5-7% productivity FY via 1:15 PM-AUM, stabilizing tech at 9 bps.

Operator: Our next question comes from Karen Wong with Barclays.

Karen Wong: What are your thoughts on the current regulatory environment and its impact on your risk profile?

Elena Vasquez: Key focus Karen. Enhanced monitoring MiFID/SFDR/T+1/Pillar Two, clawbacks LTIP, hedged overlays limit beta 60%, volatility targeting -15% drawdowns, resilient diversified book dry powder for opps, high-water marks position fee crystallization.

Operator: Thank you. There are no further questions at this time. I'd like to turn the call back over to Mark Thompson for closing remarks.

Mark Thompson: Thank you for joining us today. We appreciate your interest in Apex Asset Management. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
